greek: Καὶ ἐγένετο μετὰ τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα ὁ θεὸς ἐπείραζεν τὸν Αβρααμ καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν Αβρααμ, Αβρααμ· ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Ἰδοὺ ἐγώ.
hint: After these things God tests Abraham, calling him by name twice, and Abraham answers.

notes.text: πειράζω is first *to make proof* or *trial of*; *to try* or *tempt* a person is its second. Hebrews has Πίστει προσενήνοχεν Ἀβραὰμ τὸν Ἰσαὰκ πειραζόμενος, 11:17.
The article as a pronoun, `he`, as at 4:9.
The name is capitalised as a name, not as the first word of speech.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾăbî ʾărām*, *father of Aram*. The Greek has *father of Syrians*.
One translation, *first-born*: plain text, as at 10:15.

reading: the [[name:Ωξ]] first-born and the [[name:Βαυξ]] [[son of the same mother|a son of the same mother, a brother, a near kinsman|ἀδελφός]] of him and the [[name:Καμουηλ]] [[father|father, grandfather|πατήρ]] of [[name:Σύρων]]

names.gloss: (Ωξ, from Hebrew ʿÛṣ, of uncertain meaning)
(Βαυξ, from Hebrew Bûz, of uncertain meaning)
(Καμουηλ, from Hebrew Qĕmûʾēl, of uncertain meaning)
(Σύρος, the man of Συρία, Syria, for Hebrew ʾĂrām)

greek: καὶ τὸν Χασαδ καὶ τὸν Αζαυ καὶ τὸν Φαλδας καὶ τὸν Ιεδλαφ καὶ τὸν Βαθουηλ·
hint: More of Nahor's sons: Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph and Bethuel.

notes.text: [[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads Χασζαδ and Ιελδαφ; Rahlfs takes Χασαδ from D and Ιεδλαφ from Lagarde's edition.

reading: and the [[name:Χασαδ]] and the [[name:Αζαυ]] and the [[name:Φαλδας]] and the [[name:Ιεδλαφ]] and the [[name:Βαθουηλ]];

names.gloss: (Χασαδ, from Hebrew Keśed, of uncertain meaning)
(Αζαυ, from Hebrew Ḥăzô, of uncertain meaning)
(Φαλδας, from Hebrew Pildāš, of uncertain meaning)
(Ιεδλαφ, from Hebrew Yidlāp, of uncertain meaning)
(Βαθουηλ, from Hebrew Bĕtûʾēl, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ Βαθουηλ ἐγέννησεν τὴν Ρεβεκκαν. ὀκτὼ οὗτοι υἱοί, οὓς ἔτεκεν Μελχα τῷ Ναχωρ τῷ ἀδελφῷ Αβρααμ.
hint: Bethuel fathers Rebekah. These eight Milcah bore to Nahor, Abraham's brother.

notes.text: ὀκτώ, *eight*, plain, as at 5:4.

reading: and [[name:Βαθουηλ]] [[begot|begot / engendered, brought forth, produced|γεννάω]] the [[name:Ρεβεκκαν]]. eight [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] sons, whom [[brought into the world|brought into the world, begot, produced and yielded, brought forth, bore young / bred, laid eggs, bore / produced, generated / produced|τίκτω]] [[name:Μελχα]] to the [[name:Ναχωρ]] [[to the son of the same mother|to the son of the same mother, to the brother, to the near kinsman|ἀδελφός]] of [[name:Αβρααμ]].

names.gloss: (Ρεβεκκα, from Hebrew Ribqâ, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ ἡ παλλακὴ αὐτοῦ, ᾗ ὄνομα Ρεημα, ἔτεκεν καὶ αὐτὴ τὸν Ταβεκ καὶ τὸν Γααμ καὶ τὸν Τοχος καὶ τὸν Μωχα.
hint: Nahor's concubine Reumah also bears Tebah, Gaham, Tahash and Maacah.

notes.text: Middle Liddell's παλλακή is *= παλλακίς*: *a concubine, mistress*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone reads Ρεηρα, and Τααμ with some witnesses.

reading: and [[the concubine|the concubine / mistress|παλλακή]] of him, to whom [[a name|a name, name / fame, a mere name, a false name / pretence / pretext, a phrase / expression, a saying / speech, a noun|ὄνομα]] [[name:Ρεημα]], [[brought into the world|brought into the world, begot, produced and yielded, brought forth, bore young / bred, laid eggs, bore / produced, generated / produced|τίκτω]] [[also|also / even, and, and above all, or, but, nay, and yet, as, likewise|καί]] she the [[name:Ταβεκ]] and the [[name:Γααμ]] and the [[name:Τοχος]] and the [[name:Μωχα]].

names.gloss: (Ρεημα, from Hebrew Rĕʾûmâ, of uncertain meaning)
(Ταβεκ, from Hebrew Ṭebaḥ, of uncertain meaning)
(Γααμ, from Hebrew Gaḥam, of uncertain meaning)
(Τοχος, from Hebrew Taḥaš, of uncertain meaning)
(Μωχα, from Hebrew Maʿăkâ, of uncertain meaning)
